key_insight: OmniFabric focuses on generating coherent UV-space textures for 3D garments from a single image, aiming to produce assets that look consistent across the whole garment rather than locally plausible but globally broken. The key breakthrough is separating texture synthesis from baked-in lighting/shadows so the result is better suited for relighting and downstream simulation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the bottleneck in single-image 3D garment reconstruction: producing high-quality, globally consistent textures. Existing methods often embed lighting/shadows into the texture map or create incoherent regions, which makes the reconstructed garments difficult to use in production pipelines.
method: Synthesizes garment textures directly in UV space to preserve global coherence across the full surface.
Targets production-ready appearance by reducing unwanted baked illumination and shadow artifacts in the texture map.
Integrates texture generation with 3D garment reconstruction so the output is more usable for relighting and physical simulation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this improves the practicality of 3D asset generation by making outputs more editable, relightable, and simulation-friendly. It is especially relevant for digital fashion, virtual try-on, and content creation workflows that need reliable geometry-texture consistency.

paper_title: OmniFabric: Coherent UV Space Texture Synthesis for 3D Garment Reconstruction
paper_authors: Ding-Jiun Huang, Yuanhao Wang, Cheng Zhang, Hugo Bertiche, Alexandru-Eugen Ichim
